title: Can Automated Underwriting Help CRE Brokers?
summary: Automated underwriting helps CRE brokers close faster by extracting deal data and running key metrics. Lenders still make the final call.
body_markdown:
Yes, automated underwriting for CRE brokers speeds up deals by reading documents, pulling out the numbers, and running first-pass metrics for you. CRE means commercial real estate. The result is a cleaner package that reaches the lender ready for review, and the lender still makes the final call.


That shift matters because brokers spend much of a deal on prep work that software can now handle. Real estate underwriting software takes on the repetitive steps, so you can put more hours into finding deals and working with lenders. To see where time slips away in a typical process, learn how to[optimize your underwriting workflow](https://www.lendflow.com/post/how-to-optimize-your-underwriting-workflow-for-maximum-speed-and-accuracy) .


### Understand What Automated Underwriting Means in CRE


Underwriting is the process a lender uses to decide whether a loan is safe to make. In CRE underwriting, the lender studies a building's income, leases, expenses, and value, along with the borrower's track record.


Home loans work differently from commercial loans. Residential lenders often use an automated underwriting system (AUS) that checks a file against set rules and returns a loan recommendation. In CRE, lenders usually apply their own rules to each property, and AI underwriting tools support the people doing the analysis.


The clearest way to understand the split is to see which jobs belong to software and which belong to people:


- **Software reads:** It sorts uploaded files and labels each document type.
- **Software extracts:** It pulls rents, expenses, and lease dates into organized fields.
- **Software models:** It calculates first-pass metrics from the extracted numbers.
- **People set assumptions:** Brokers and analysts choose vacancy, rent growth, and expense figures.
- **People decide:** The lender's credit team approves the loan, declines it, or changes the terms.


### Cut the Manual Work That Slows Brokers Down


Manual underwriting means people handle every step by hand, from requesting files to typing numbers into a spreadsheet. For brokers, that work tends to pile up in the same few places on almost every deal:


- **Document chasing:** You email borrowers again and again for missing leases, tax returns, or bank statements.
- **Retyping rent rolls:** You copy a rent roll, which lists each tenant, rent, and lease date, into a spreadsheet line by line.
- **Rebuilding T-12s:** You reformat the T-12, a report of the last 12 months of income and expenses, so a lender can read it.
- **Typing errors:** One wrong digit can change the cash flow and hurt your credibility with a lender.
- **Lender back-and-forth:** Each question about a number sends the file back to you and restarts the clock.


Lendflow's guide to[AI document automation in lending](https://www.lendflow.com/post/no-more-manual-entry-ai-document-automation-in-lending) explains why paperwork is the bottleneck that shows up across loan types. The same problem hits CRE brokers, because every deal depends on a stack of property and borrower documents.


Lenders also have good reasons to read CRE files closely. The[FDIC 2026 Risk Review](https://www.fdic.gov/analysis/2026-risk-review-full.pdf) reports that "The banking industry's median CRE loan concentration ratio was 200 percent" at the end of 2025.


That ratio compares a bank's CRE loans to its tier 1 capital plus its allowance for credit losses. Together, those two amounts act as the bank's cushion against losses.


The FDIC found the ratio ran higher at smaller banks, with a 311 percent median for banks holding $1 billion to $10 billion in assets. It also noted that overall CRE delinquencies and charge-offs stayed low, though results were uneven across bank groups. For brokers, the practical lesson is simple: clear, well-sourced underwriting reports make a careful lender's review easier.


### Speak the Lender's Language With Five Core CRE Metrics


Most CRE underwriting automation tools calculate the same core metrics, and lenders use them to size and price a loan. Knowing what each one means helps you spot a weak deal before a lender does.


Metric Plain definition Simple formula Why lenders care


Net operating income (NOI) Income left after operating costs, before loan payments Total income minus operating expenses Shows how much cash the property produces


Debt service coverage ratio (DSCR) How many times NOI covers the yearly loan payments NOI ÷ annual loan payments Shows whether the property can carry the loan


Capitalization (cap) rate The yearly return on a property's value, ignoring any loan NOI ÷ property value Helps estimate and compare property values


Occupancy The share of space or units that tenants lease Leased space ÷ total space Shows how steady the income is


Debt yield NOI as a share of the loan amount NOI ÷ loan amount Shows risk without depending on rate or loan term


Here is a quick example of how these numbers work together. A property with $500,000 in NOI and $400,000 in yearly loan payments has a DSCR of 1.25. That means its income covers the loan payments 1.25 times.


### Win Back Time in Four Broker Workflows


Automated underwriting for CRE brokers helps most in four places along the path from first call to lender decision. Each one removes a manual step that used to sit on your desk or your borrower's.


#### Collect and Extract Documents With Less Manual Effort


Doc Analyzer cuts "manual effort by up to 70%," according to the[Lendflow Automate launch announcement](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/lendflow-launches-ai-automation-suite-160000701.html) from August 2025. Document automation for underwriting starts with three jobs: sort each file, flag what is missing, and pull key fields into organized data.


[AI document processing with Doc Analyzer](https://www.lendflow.com/solutions/doc-analyzer) identifies, classifies, and extracts data from lending documents such as bank statements and tax returns. Instead of opening every PDF, your team sees which documents arrived and which ones still need follow-up. Doc Analyzer is part of[Lendflow Automate](https://www.lendflow.com/lendflow-automate) , a set of AI-powered tools that streamline lending operations and borrower communication.


#### Screen Deals Before They Reach a Lender


Once the data is extracted, a tool can run quick NOI and DSCR checks against your target lender's usual minimums. If the DSCR falls short, you learn that before spending a week packaging a file the lender would turn down.


Automation also catches numbers that do not match. An offering memorandum (OM) is the marketing package for a property. It might show higher rents than the T-12 supports, and a side-by-side check flags that gap so you can fix or explain it.


#### Help Lenders Decide Faster


A credit memo is the report an analyst writes to recommend a loan to the lender's credit committee. In December 2024, McKinsey studied AI systems that draft credit memos at banks. The[McKinsey AI in banking](https://www.mckinsey.com/industries/financial-services/our-insights/extracting-value-from-ai-in-banking-rewiring-the-enterprise) analysis found "credit analyst productivity gains of 20 to 60 percent, depending on various factors, and roughly 30 percent faster decision making."


That analysis covers bank credit memos in general, not CRE loans, and McKinsey describes these multi-agent systems as still nascent. Even so, a complete and well-organized package gives a lender's analysts, and any tools they use, less to fix before a decision.


#### Keep Borrowers Moving With Automated Follow-Up


Files often stall because a borrower forgets to send one document. Automated reminders and document requests go out on a schedule, so you stop writing the same email three times.


Lendflow's[AI-powered communications](https://www.lendflow.com/solutions/ai-communications) tools use voice, email, SMS, and chat to reach borrowers at the right moment. AI agents also cover routine status checks, which frees your team for the complex questions that need a person.


### Get Ready for Rising CRE Loan Volume


The Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA) tracks how many commercial loans are due each year. Its[MBA loan maturity survey](https://newslink.mba.org/mba-newslinks/2026/february/mba-newslink-tuesday-feb-10-2026/17-of-commercial-and-multifamily-mortgage-balances-to-mature-in-2026/) reports: "Seventeen percent ($875 billion) of $5.0 trillion of outstanding commercial mortgages held by lenders and investors is scheduled to mature in 2026, a 9% decrease from the $957 billion that was scheduled to mature in 2025."


A maturity is the date a loan comes due, and these are scheduled amounts based on balances at the end of 2025. Scheduled does not mean every loan will refinance or default, and MBA notes that balances at maturity will generally be lower.


New lending also grew. The[MBA 2025 origination report](https://newslink.mba.org/cmf-newslinks/2026/april/mba-commercial-multifamily-newslink-thursday-april-30-2026/mba-annual-report-finds-total-commercial-real-estate-borrowing-and-lending-increased-40-in-2025/) states: "Total commercial real estate mortgage borrowing and lending is estimated to have totaled $706 billion in 2025, a 40% increase from the $505 billion in 2024." That figure is an estimate for the whole US market, not a count of broker deals.


AI use in CRE is still early. The 2027[Deloitte commercial real estate outlook](https://www.deloitte.com/us/en/insights/industry/financial-services/financial-services-industry-outlooks/commercial-real-estate-outlook.html) reports: "Ninety-two percent of the surveyed respondents are in the piloting or research phase, while only 8% have integrated AI solutions." Deloitte surveyed 950 executives at CRE owners and investors worldwide in mid-2026, not brokers or lenders.


Our own read is that more scheduled maturities and more lending likely mean more files to package. Brokers who automate prep work early can handle that load without adding staff at the same pace.


### Keep Human Judgment Where It Counts


Beyond the lender's credit decision, several parts of a CRE deal still need trained people. Software can support these steps, but it should not own them:


- **Appraisal:** A licensed appraiser sets the property's value in a report the lender relies on.
- **Title review:** A title company confirms ownership and finds liens, which are legal claims against the property.
- **Site inspection:** Someone must walk the property to see the roof, systems, and surroundings that no spreadsheet shows.
- **Legal review:** Attorneys check leases, loan documents, and zoning, which are local rules on how land can be used.
- **Broker relationships:** Lenders return calls from brokers they trust, and that trust is built person to person.


Like any AI tool, automated underwriting for CRE brokers is not always accurate. A blurry scan, an unusual lease format, or a merged spreadsheet cell can produce a wrong number. Someone should check every extracted figure against its source before a file goes out.


### Choose a Tool That Fits Your Deal Flow


Use this checklist when you compare real estate underwriting software. The right fit matches the documents you see most and the lenders you send deals to.


Criterion What to ask Why it matters


Traceability Can I click a number and see the page it came from? Lets you check figures and answer lender questions fast


Input fit Does it read my rent rolls, T-12s, OMs, and scanned PDFs? A tool that misreads your files creates more work


Editable outputs Can I change assumptions and export to a spreadsheet? Lenders want to see and adjust your math


Integrations Does it connect to my CRM, email, and file storage? Fewer handoffs mean fewer lost documents


Human review Can I approve or correct extracted data before it is used? Keeps a person in charge of accuracy


Trial access Can I test it on my own past deals? Shows real results before you commit


For a deeper set of vendor questions, read Lendflow's guide on[how to choose AI underwriting tools](https://www.lendflow.com/post/ai-underwriting-tools-for-sba-lenders-how-to-choose-one-that-speeds-decisions-without-adding-risk) . It is written for lenders of Small Business Administration (SBA) loans, but its checks on speed and risk apply to CRE tools too.


### Turn Automation Into a Competitive Edge


AI use keeps spreading across business. The[McKinsey state of AI](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/quantumblack/our-insights/the-state-of-ai-2025) survey found "88 percent report regular AI use in at least one business function, compared with 78 percent a year ago." That 2025 global survey covered nearly 2,000 respondents across all industries, and only about one-third said their companies had begun to scale AI.


With automated underwriting for CRE brokers, the edge comes from using it well while many firms are still testing AI:


- **More deals per broker:** Less time retyping documents means more time sourcing and packaging new deals.
- **Faster responses:** You can answer a lender's question with a sourced number instead of digging through email.
- **Lender credibility:** Consistent, clean packages show lenders that your files are ready for review.

### Frequently Asked Questions About Automated Underwriting


These short answers cover common questions from brokers who are new to automated underwriting.


#### Can AI Underwrite a CRE Deal End to End?


No, AI can read documents, extract data, and run first-pass metrics, but appraisals, inspections, legal review, and the final credit decision still need people.


#### Does AI Underwriting Replace Analysts or Credit Officers?


No, it shifts their time from data entry to judgment. Analysts review what the tool produces, and credit officers still approve or decline the loan.


#### What Does a CRE Underwriter Do?


A CRE underwriter studies a property's income, expenses, leases, and value to decide whether a loan fits the lender's risk rules. The underwriter also reviews the borrower's experience and finances, then writes a recommendation for the credit committee, often in a credit memo.


#### How Long Does Automated Underwriting Take?


There is no standard time benchmark for CRE, because timing depends on how complete the file is and how quickly the lender reviews it. Extraction and first-pass metrics can run soon after documents arrive, but missing files and lender questions still set the pace.


#### What Are the Three Types of Underwriting?


The three main types are loan underwriting, insurance underwriting, and securities underwriting. CRE brokers work with loan underwriting, where a lender decides whether to fund a property loan.
